Based on my review of the Quzhou County survey data, I now have a solid understanding of typical farming practices for a smallholder in this region. Let me provide my answer as the farmer.

---

I am 44 years old and have been farming in Quzhou County since I was a teenager. My family has about 6.5 mu of land, and I manage it with help from my husband when he's not working odd jobs in town. I finished middle school, so I can do my own cost calculations and read seed labels — that matters when the dealers try to push expensive stuff on you.

My wheat went in last October on 5 mu — I sowed improved *shimai 22* at about 30 jin per mu. Right now in April, the wheat is greening up and this is the critical time. I will topdress it with urea and run border irrigation from our well three more times before harvest in early June. I'll spray twice for insects and once for weeds. This wheat-maize rotation is my backbone; it's reliable, the grain station always buys it, and I know exactly what every mu costs me.

After the wheat comes off in June, I will plant maize on those same 5 mu. I use no-tillage direct seeding now — the machine drills right into the wheat stubble. Saves diesel and time. I buy *Denghai 605* hybrid seed, about one package per mu, and put down 28-6-6 compound fertilizer at planting, roughly 100 jin per mu. The maize needs two irrigations and three pesticide sprays. Expected yield is around 1,150 jin per mu if the weather cooperates.

On my remaining 1.5 mu, I am planting cotton this year. I will rotary-till that plot, lay plastic mulch, and sow *guoxinmian* hybrid seed in April. Cotton is more work — pruning, lots of spraying — but it brings cash I can use directly for household expenses. I apply compound fertilizer as basal and topdress once. Cotton needs three irrigations and about eight pesticide applications because the bollworms are always a problem here. I expect about 500 jin per mu.

I do not grow vegetables or stevia like some of the bigger family farms. Those crops are risky — one bad price or one heavy rain and you watch your money rot in the field. Wheat, maize, and cotton I can always sell, and I understand their temperaments. That is my plan.
